sources.entry: QuickShare - Quick and simple file sharing between different devices. (Source Code) LGPL-3.0 Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: QuickShare is a self-hostable, browser-based file sharing and management server for moving files between devices, written in Go with a Node.js/Yarn front end.
summary.what_it_does: QuickShare lets you upload, download, create, delete and move files and folders through a web browser. It supports fuzzy search across files and folders, resumable uploads and downloads, and uploading hundreds of files at once. You can share directories with others, including anonymously, and open sharing folders by scanning a QR code. The server supports multiple users with roles (user/admin), per-user home directories, per-user upload and download speed limits, and per-user space quotas. The README also says streaming upload is supported so it can work behind a CDN or reverse proxy, that files can be managed directly from the OS, and that it runs on Linux, Mac and Windows.
use_cases: share files between my computers and phones
host a private file sharing server for a small team
give others temporary or anonymous access to a folder
upload many files to a server from a browser
set per-user storage quotas on a shared server
run a self-hosted file server behind a reverse proxy
how_to_run: docker run --name quickshare -d -p 8686:8686 -v `pwd`/quickshare/root:/quickshare/root -e DEFAULTADMIN=qs -e DEFAULTADMINPWD=1234 hexxa/quickshare
Or download a release executable and run: DEFAULTADMIN=qs DEFAULTADMINPWD=1234 ./quickshare
Open the web UI in a browser and log in with user name qs and password 1234
notable: Resumable uploads and downloads in the browser
Per-user upload/download speed limits and space quotas
Share directories anonymously and via QR code
Files can also be managed directly from the OS filesystem
Ships as a single executable or Docker image
caveats: README warns the project is under active development and full backward compatibility is not guaranteed
Default credentials (qs / 1234) are shown in examples and must be changed for any real deployment
